name: Dungbeetle
label: Widesound
lede: Two Brown graduates started a band in Providence in the summer of 1990 and took it to the Lower East Side, where their singer wore a cape, called himself Sam Shit and never once winked. They left one 7-inch and a soundtrack song, then played again exactly once, in 2014.

eras.title: Upstairs from Sleepyhead
eras.text: Two Brown graduates, Sam Lipsyte and Nick Butterworth, stay in Providence after graduation and spend the summer of 1990 starting a band on Prospect Street. By fall they've taken it to the Lower East Side.

years.cap: Nick Butterworth and Sam Lipsyte on the Prospect Street porch, Providence, c. 1990 · Photo: Michael Galinsky
years.src: Michael Galinsky: More Dungbeetle · Rumur: Galinsky memoir · Wikipedia: Sam Lipsyte
years.h: Two Brown grads stay in Providence to start a band
years.p: Sam Lipsyte and Nick Butterworth live upstairs from Sleepyhead, who are subletting the floor below on Prospect Street. Sleepyhead's Michael Galinsky is the neighbor with the camera.
years.xp:
Galinsky remembers them as "2 Brown students who had stuck around after graduation to start their band." That summer he and Lipsyte also sketched out a film idea in the spirit of Slacker.

Galinsky calls his own memory of that summer "more metaphorical than factual," so the year comes from the graduations: Lipsyte and guitarist Rob Reynolds both finished at Brown in 1990.

years.h: Named for a bug that rolls its dinner uphill
years.p: Lipsyte's explanation of the name, to the Village Voice: dung beetles "spend their lives rolling in shit uphill."

years.h: The drummer is their semiotics TA
years.p: "We got our semiotics TA to be our drummer," Lipsyte told the Paris Review, dating the band to "'90, '91, right out of undergrad." He doesn't name the TA.

years.src: Michael Galinsky: CBGB backstage with Velvet Crush · Vulture · Crack · Wikipedia: Rob Reynolds · NY Mag
years.h: The band moves to the Lower East Side
years.p: Lipsyte and Butterworth head to New York and crash at Sleepyhead's Chris's place on 2nd Street between A and B. Brown classmate Rob Reynolds plays guitar.
years.xp:
Reynolds, an art and semiotics graduate who did the Whitney Independent Study Program in 1992, later listed his bandmates as "Sam Lipsyte, Big Jimmy Fingers and Bruce Oyster Cooley." Nobody has said in print who Big Jimmy Fingers is.

New York Magazine says Butterworth went on to figure prominently in the dot-com boom.

eras.title: Against flannel
eras.text: In the year of plaid shirts, the singer called himself Sam Shit, wore a cape and refused to let the audience in on the joke. CBGB, a college show and a new sound man followed.

years.cap: Sam Lipsyte takes flight at CBGB, 1991, with Rob Bingham watching from the wings · Photo: Michael Galinsky
years.h: Lipsyte takes the stage as Sam Shit, in a cape
years.p: "I might have worn a cape. We were against flannel," Lipsyte told the Paris Review. His mic rode in a tool belt covered in purple glitter.
years.xp:
Lipsyte called it "the glamorous made abject." He liked to tell crowds things like "You have a choice, police state or police state."

To the Observer, years later: "I liked the idea that I couldn't really be understood." In his own job description he was "the lead singer/screamer/deadpan tummler."

q: one of the most influential bands on me ever
years.src: Pitchfork · NY Mag · Crack · RBMA · Substack
years.h: A sound guy from Spiral starts mixing their shows
years.p: [[James Murphy|6b70c46c-5c83-4cc7-99c1-e76b68919c6a]] signs on to run sound; Pitchfork calls the band his first sound-engineer clients. With them he builds his first real studio, on a desolate block in Dumbo, at $375 a month.
years.xp:
Reynolds met Murphy when he "was the sound guy at a club called Spiral." The studio, Plantain Recording House, lasted until Murphy was evicted in 1995. Lipsyte remembers a Serbian truck driver next door painting slogans like "NO ABILITY TO LOVE, NO CAPACITY TO FORGIVE."

When the band couldn't find its drummer for a wedding gig ("working for FEMA or something," Murphy said), Murphy sat in, learned their cover of Harry Nilsson's Jump Into the Fire and later took it to his own band. Lipsyte says Dungbeetle introduced him to Juan MacLean; the two co-produced a Dungbeetle recording and "hated each other."

years.cap: Sam Lipsyte with Dungbeetle at Amherst College, 1991 · Photo: Tae Won Yu
years.h: The act goes on the road to Amherst College
years.p: A college show in western Massachusetts, caught by photographer Tae Won Yu. Vulture ran the picture in its 2013 Lipsyte profile.

years.h: Lipsyte finds the meanest man in the room and strokes his cheek
years.p: His own description, to Jewcy: walk into the crowd, pick out "the meanest, most homophobic looking dude" and stroke his cheek gently.
years.xp:
"The band was very noisy," Lipsyte said. "Our stage show was very much about denying audiences that moment, that sort of wink that makes everything okay."

To the Paris Review he put it flatter: "There was no wink, and that was our actual credo."

years.cap: Sam Lipsyte and Velvet Crush's John Davis backstage at CBGB, Nick Butterworth behind, c. 1991 · Photo: Michael Galinsky
years.src: Michael Galinsky: CBGB backstage with Velvet Crush
years.h: CBGB books Dungbeetle with Velvet Crush
years.p: Galinsky's backstage frame from the night ("91 probably," he wrote) has Lipsyte laughing with [[Velvet Crush|dadd10f1-9db4-4a35-b939-9469029deab5]]'s John Davis in the graffiti room.

eras.title: One single, no more
eras.text: The band put out exactly one record, a three-song 7-inch, and played a scattering of rooms on and around Avenue B. Galinsky later counted fewer New York shows than eggs in a partly used carton.

yt: Blow Hole (the Destroyer A-side, from the Scraps CD)
years.h: Destroyer is the only record they ever release
years.p: Three songs on a Widesound 7-inch: Blowhole on the A-side, Swinger and Temptation on the flip. Discogs lists no players.
years.xp: Per the Discogs notes, the B-side was recorded at Waterworks in New York and Blowhole at Snack Time in Hoboken; the copyright line reads Rhizome Press. Vulture remembers their "big" single being cut in a Dumbo loft instead, and the sleeve doesn't settle it.

years.h: Six Finger Satellite plays big brother
years.p: Lipsyte calls the Providence band "sort of a big brother band to us. We played with them a lot." One night the bill was with [[The Jesus Lizard|dfebd6c0-dae7-4cc8-a8e9-0dbaa382209f]].

years.h: Other bands drop the theater; Dungbeetle writes rock operas
years.p: Lipsyte's subjects included Ham the space chimp, Evel Knievel and something called "Prophets of Rock."
years.xp: Lipsyte says he was "never much of a musician... I learned some chords and wrote a few of our songs." In the studio he once cut a vocal take naked, "because I thought it would make the performance more intense and vulnerable, but I think it had the opposite effect."

years.h: Gargoyle Mechanique on Avenue B becomes "a total inferno"
years.p: Galinsky's memory of the show: roaring, with a thrown beer bottle hitting someone in the audience.

years.src: I Miss Lounge Ax · Michael Galinsky: Pyramid loft bill
years.h: No PA for the vocals at the loft above the Pyramid Club
years.p: Playing before [[Rodan|1e9250c4-46d2-48f1-b7c7-5f1c0a6b1abd]] in Murphy's loft on Avenue A, Lipsyte picks up the louder floor monitor and sings the rest of the set with it hung from his neck, facing out.
years.xp:
Rodan's [[Jeff Mueller|06502a8d-ae1a-4ca4-ab28-07fa3582597e]] tells it, dating it "1992ish": "there wasn't enough PA for Sam's vocals, so, he picked up the louder floor monitor and played the rest of the show with it sorta strapped around his neck facing out."

Sleepyhead and Pony were on the loft bill too, per Galinsky.

years.cap: A handwritten "DuNG Beetle" cassette in a stack of '90s demo tapes · Photo: Jonathan Hills
years.h: A tape marked "DuNG Beetle" survives in a stack of demos
years.p: The handwritten cassette sits with demos by Big Bomb and Johnson Noise in a photo posted in 2015 as "The demo years."

eras.title: Gas money
eras.text: Sleepyhead took them west for about ten days, which Galinsky thinks was very likely their only tour. Chicago was the good night; very few of the other shows paid enough for gas.

years.cap: Dungbeetle rehearsing at Tu Casa, Avenue B and 6th Street, c. 1993 · Photo: Michael Galinsky
years.h: Galinsky shoots a rehearsal at Tu Casa on Avenue B
years.p: His verdict on the band in that room: "Heavy, fractured, mildly dangerous." He thinks his are some of the only pictures anyone took of them.
years.xp: Galinsky says the Midwest tour came "later that year," and that Jcx Esq. did some of the driving.

years.cap: Sam Lipsyte out on the floor at Lounge Ax, Chicago, January 1993, shot from the stage · Photo: Michael Galinsky
years.src: Michael Galinsky: Lounge Ax · I Miss Lounge Ax
years.h: At Lounge Ax, Lipsyte goes out and drags the crowd forward
years.p: Opening for Sleepyhead in Chicago. "Sam would go out and pull them forward," Galinsky wrote; a fan citing The List dates it January 31, 1993.
years.xp: Galinsky's pick for anyone listening now: The Man Went Out, the song that later landed on the Half-Cocked soundtrack.

years.cap: Dungbeetle on stage at Lounge Ax, Chicago, c. 1993 · Photo: Michael Galinsky
years.src: Michael Galinsky: Midwest tour · Rumur: Half-Cocked
years.h: Ten days in the Midwest, rarely enough for gas
years.p: "Very few shows paid enough for gas money," Galinsky wrote of the run with Sleepyhead. "I remember that Chicago was special."
years.xp: In Chattanooga they played with Big Heifer. "It hadn't been a very good crowd, but it was a good show," Galinsky wrote. Sleepyhead made a habit of it, helping bands like Ruby Falls and Dungbeetle get out of town.

years.h: In a Columbus bagel shop, Lipsyte pours candle wax on his head
years.p: On what Galinsky calls the "pig nation tour," at a show booked by Bela, Lipsyte jumped on a table, grabbed its candle and poured the wax on his forehead.

eras.title: Chaos, then competency
eras.text: By 1994 the band was coming apart. One more song made it onto a record, on Matador, and the date of the last show isn't on record.

years.h: Dungbeetle starts to dissolve
years.p: Lipsyte's theory, from 2023: they began as "a kind of inspired chaos outfit" and ended able to "deliver a pretty tight, punishing set."
years.xp:
Vulture dates the end to 1994. Lipsyte had expected it, telling the Observer the band would probably fall apart, "And that's exactly what happened."

The 2014 reunion was billed as their first live performance in 19 years, which puts the last show around 1995.

years.h: The Man Went Out lands on Matador's Half-Cocked
years.p: The film is Suki Hawley and Galinsky's; Dungbeetle's 2:44 sits at track 18 of the CD. Lipsyte says the drummer wasn't feeling well that day.

eras.title: Sam Shit goes to print
eras.text: The singer became a novelist, the guitarist a painter, and the band survived as a song on a photo book's CD and a line in author profiles.

years.h: Galinsky's Scraps brings back Blow Hole
years.p: The 80-page photo book comes with a CD: Dungbeetle at track 2, alongside [[Yo La Tengo|3f542031-b054-454d-b57b-812fa2a81b11]], Sleepyhead and [[Dump|2d9215eb-0d46-4624-b155-2a0f32482a4e]]. Lipsyte writes one of the essays.
years.xp: Covering the Scraps show at CB's Gallery in March 1999, the Village Voice noted that Lipsyte once "operated as Sam Shit in something called Dungbeetle." It quoted his essay: "Things rock in the context of what they promise to do, and how they betray that."

years.h: The screamer publishes Venus Drive
years.p: Lipsyte's first book arrives, then The Subject Steve, Home Land and The Ask. He ends up teaching fiction at Columbia.

years.h: An n+1 podcast signs off with a rare Dungbeetle recording
years.p: Lipsyte is the guest on the magazine's second episode, which ends on the band.

q: He was like a charismatic cult leader.
years.h: Reynolds: "a cross between Lemmy Kilmister and Andy Kaufman"
years.p: In Vulture's profile of Lipsyte, his old guitarist adds: "You could never tell if he was joking or serious."
years.xp: Reynolds, by then a painter, gave Vulture the other half of the picture: Lipsyte on stage was "like a charismatic cult leader." The same profile ran Tae Won Yu's 1991 photo of Lipsyte at Amherst.

eras.title: Nineteen years, one night
eras.text: Dungbeetle came back exactly once, for a magazine party on Bleecker Street, with their old sound man on drums. After that the band lived on in a novel and in the friendship between its singer and its guitarist.

years.cap: Sam Lipsyte fronts the reunited Dungbeetle at Le Poisson Rouge, November 22, 2014
years.src: LPR · Stereogum · Radio Silence · Hollandude · Pancakes and Whiskey
years.h: Nineteen years on, Dungbeetle plays Le Poisson Rouge
years.p: The Radio Silence issue-three party reunites Lipsyte, Reynolds and Butterworth, with James Murphy on drums. Stereogum notes it's Murphy's first live set since LCD Soundsystem ended in 2011.
years.xp: Tickets were $39.50, and the bill also had [[Stephin Merritt|fec52bf2-450e-4ca7-a517-c3f2097d964c]], Tanya Donelly, Greil Marcus and Rick Moody. One review called the set "honest and loud"; Pancakes and Whiskey said the band "rocked the stage ridiculously and without any manners."

years.h: Reynolds's painting UP! becomes an LCD Soundsystem cover
years.p: The old Dungbeetle guitarist, now painting in Los Angeles, supplies the cover of American Dream.
years.xp: Reynolds told LA Weekly he left New York for LA "kicking and screaming."

years.h: Lipsyte puts a Lower East Side band of 1993 in a novel
years.p: No One Left to Come Looking for You follows a rock bassist and his bandmates. The Boston Globe says it "started as real experience."
years.xp: Reynolds and [[Craig Wedren|2da87294-e651-420b-8d25-2dbc3b29a285]] made the intro and outro music for the audiobook. Reynolds's congratulations called Lipsyte his "Dearest friend and Dungbeetle bandmate."

yt: Rob Reynolds and Sam Lipsyte, Artforum
years.h: The painter and the novelist talk shop for Artforum
years.p: Reynolds and Lipsyte, who met at Brown and moved to New York together, sit down for Artforum's "Artists on Writers | Writers on Artists."

years.h: "Dungbeetle was home, a kind of anchor"
years.p: Lipsyte, looking back for Martin McKenzie-Murray. In music, he added, Murphy "was in the first group, and I was in the third."
